paper.title: A Closer Look at the Worst-case Behavior of Multi-armed Bandit Algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed stochastic bandit with rewards in [0,1]
unmapped: instance gap allowed to scale with the horizon n (triangular-array asymptotics)
settings.definition_quote: The arms are indexed by $\{1,2\}$. Each arm~$i\in\{1,2\}$ is characterized by a reward distribution $\mathcal{P}_i$ supported on $[0,1]$ with mean $\mu_i$. ... The rewards are assumed to be i.i.d. in time, and independent across arms.

symbols.theta_gap: fixed constant theta >= 0 such that the gap Delta ~ sqrt(theta log n / n)

conditions: gap scales as Delta ~ sqrt(theta*log(n)/n) for fixed theta >= 0

source.label: cor
source.quote: In the ``moderate gap'' regime referenced in Theorem~\ref{thm:rates} where $\Delta\sim\sqrt{\frac{\theta\log n}{n}}$, the (stochastic) regret of the policy $\pi$ given by Algorithm~\ref{alg:UCB} initialized with $\rho>1$ satisfies as $n\to\infty$, $\frac{R_n^\pi}{\sqrt{n\log n}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\theta}\left( 1 - \lambda_\rho^{\ast}(\theta) \right) =: h_\rho(\theta)$

results.notes: This is a sharp limit in law (convergence in probability) of the stochastic regret normalised by sqrt(n log n), not an upper bound. The closed form of h_rho comes from Appendix A. Maximising over theta gives the worst-case constant: R_n ~ h_rho(theta*_rho) sqrt(n log n). Theorem 1 (the arm-sampling rate N_i*(n)/n -> lambda*_rho(theta), 1/2, or 1) and Theorem 2 (the K-armed uniform split over the optimal arms) are limit results on sampling rates and are not recorded as regret results.

bound.regime: diffusion scaling: mu_i = mu + theta_i/sqrt(T), Delta = Delta_0/sqrt(T), T -> infinity

symbols.Delta_0: |theta_1 - theta_2|, the diffusion-scaled gap, so Delta = Delta_0/sqrt(T)

conditions: mu_i = mu + theta_i/sqrt(n) with fixed constants mu, theta_1, theta_2 >= 0

source.label: thm:diffusion
source.quote: Suppose that the mean reward of arm~$i\in\{1,2\}$ is given by $\mu_i = \mu + \theta_i/\sqrt{n}$ ... Then, the following process-level convergences hold under the policy $\pi$ given by Algorithm~\ref{alg:UCB} initialized with $\rho>1$: ... (II) $\left( \frac{R^{\pi}_{\left\lfloor nt \right\rfloor}}{\sqrt{n}} \right) \Rightarrow \left( \frac{\Delta_0t}{2} + \sqrt{\frac{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}{2}}\tilde{B}(t) \right)$

results.notes: This is a process-level weak-convergence result. At t = 1, R_n/sqrt(n) is asymptotically Gaussian with mean Delta_0/2 and variance (sigma_1^2+sigma_2^2)/2. The recorded expression is the mean of the limit, rescaled to total regret: Delta_0*sqrt(n)/2 = Delta*n/2. The Gaussian fluctuations are of order sqrt(n). Part (I) gives the Brownian limit of the cumulative reward processes.
